jurisdiction.name: Saudi Arabia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Saudi Arabia governs AI mainly through SDAIA, which leads the National Strategy for Data & AI (2020) and is also the personal-data regulator. The approach is guidance-led rather than legislation-led: there is no AI-specific statute in force. Instead, a layered set of SDAIA principles and frameworks covers ethics (2023, updated 2025), generative AI (2024), deepfakes (2026), AI adoption and bias. Binding obligations come mainly from the Personal Data Protection Law, in force since September 2023. Sector bodies are adding their own layers: SFDA for medical AI, CST for tech companies, NCA for AI cybersecurity (draft). Current direction is toward hard law for AI infrastructure (draft Global AI Hub Law, 2025) and measurement of government AI readiness through the National AI Index.
lead_institutions: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
narrative.review_notes: Pilot deep review. The websites of the Saudi Data and AI Authority and the Bureau of Experts' legal portal could not be read automatically; dates were checked against official announcements, the national consultation platform and the cybersecurity, standards and food and drug authorities. Occupational standards and an academic qualifications framework for AI were reviewed and not recorded. AI principles for the media sector (2026) are pending until an official document is published.

instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Published guidance. Month of publication taken from a secondary tracker; the official document page blocks automated access.
instruments.summary: Guidance for government entities on adopting generative AI tools responsibly. It sets out use cases, risks (data leakage, misinformation, bias, IP) and the controls entities should apply, aligned with the AI Ethics Principles. Applies to public-sector bodies; no binding effect is stated.

instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Launched at the Global AI Summit, Riyadh, 21 October 2020; led by SDAIA.
instruments.summary: National strategy to make Saudi Arabia a global leader in data and AI by 2030. It is organised around six dimensions: ambition, skills, policy and regulation, investment, research and innovation, and ecosystem. It is the umbrella strategy for SDAIA-led AI governance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing strategy & action plans.

instruments.english_title: Draft adoption of ISO/IEC 5339:2024 — AI application guidance
instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO)
instruments.current_status: Public comment on proposed adoption 2025/493 ran 24 Jul – 23 Sep 2025; final adoption not yet confirmed.
instruments.summary: SASO proposal to adopt ISO/IEC 5339:2024 as a Saudi standard. The standard gives guidance on identifying the context, opportunities and processes for developing and applying AI, including stakeholder roles and life-cycle relationships. Adoption outcome after the comment period is not yet confirmed.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing standards & certification.

instruments.official_title: إطار تبني الذكاء الاصطناعي
instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Launched at the Global AI Summit on 12 Sep 2024; full document released 1 Dec 2024. The current PDF is labelled as the 2025 edition.
instruments.summary: Framework guiding public- and private-sector organisations through AI adoption: setting priorities, establishing AI units, assessing maturity (Emerging, Developed, Proficient, Advanced), and building data, technology and skills enablers. It embeds the national AI Ethics Principles. Encourages government entities to set up dedicated AI units.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing government ai governance, public-sector ai, indices & maturity.

instruments.official_title: AI Ethics Principles
instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Version 1.0 published September 2023 (draft consulted in 2022); a 2025 edition is on SDAIA's site. Binding effect is not established by the text reviewed.
instruments.summary: National AI ethics principles covering fairness, privacy and security, humanity, social and environmental benefit, reliability and safety, transparency and explainability, and accountability. They apply across the AI life cycle to entities developing or using AI in the Kingdom, with risk-based controls.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing responsible ai & ethics, risk & assurance.

instruments.official_title: نظام حماية البيانات الشخصية
instruments.issuing_authority: Council of Ministers; Royal Decree M/19 (9/2/1443H). Regulator: SDAIA
instruments.publisher_name: Bureau of Experts at the Council of Ministers
instruments.current_status: In force since 14 Sep 2023 after amendment by Royal Decree M/148 (5/9/1444H); one-year compliance grace period ended 14 Sep 2024.
instruments.summary: Comprehensive personal data protection law governing collection, processing, disclosure and cross-border transfer of personal data, with data-subject rights and controller obligations. It applies to AI training and use whenever personal data is involved, and is supervised by SDAIA. Implementing Regulations and transfer regulations accompany it.

instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Published guidance (SPA, 11 Jan 2024).
instruments.summary: Guidance for the private sector, non-profits and individuals on safe and ethical use of generative AI tools, built on seven principles. It warns against data leakage, misinformation, deepfakes and bias, and requires compliance with personal-data and IP law.

instruments.official_title: Deepfakes Guidelines: Mitigating Risks While Fostering Innovation
instruments.issuing_authority: Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Final guidelines issued 8 May 2026 after public consultation opened 11 Sep 2024.
instruments.summary: Defines deepfakes and sets requirements for developers and content creators, covering consent, disclosure and labelling, and preventing misuse for fraud, misinformation and identity theft. It builds on the AI Ethics Principles and balances legitimate creative uses against harm.

instruments.current_status: Published for public consultation on Istitlaa (page last updated 14 Apr 2025). Adoption not confirmed as of this review.
instruments.summary: Draft law creating three types of AI/data-centre hubs: Private Hubs for foreign governments, plus Extended and Virtual Hubs for operators and service providers. It sets out their legal jurisdiction and compliance regime while protecting national security and sovereignty. It is not binding unless adopted.

instruments.english_title: Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI in General Education
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education, with the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA)
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Education on 24/07/1446 AH (24 January 2025) per its own news page, which links the guide (39-page PDF, cover dated 2025, Ministry of Education and SDAIA logos).
instruments.summary: Ministry of Education guidebook, prepared with SDAIA, on the use of generative AI tools in Saudi general (school) education, addressed to students, teachers and parents. It explains how generative AI works and its benefits and risks, then sets usage rules: students under 13 should not use generative AI tools and those aged 13-18 need parental consent; AI-generated content used in assignments must be disclosed and cited, and non-disclosure is treated as academic dishonesty; outputs must be checked for bias and errors. A third part covers prompt-writing principles.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Saudi ministry-level instrument shaping AI use (sectoral, generative-ai, ethics).

instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Media, with the Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority (SDAIA), the General Authority for Media Regulation, the Saudi Broadcasting Authority and the Saudi Media Forum
instruments.current_status: Published on SDAIA's AI page in Arabic and English (cover: 2026, classification Public; logos of the Ministry of Media, SDAIA, the General Authority for Media Regulation, the Saudi Broadcasting Authority and the Saudi Media Forum). Previously held as a lead. English version: https://sdaia.gov.sa/en/MediaCenter/KnowledgeCenter/ResearchLibrary/AIPrinciplesMedia.pdf
instruments.summary: Sector principles for the use of AI across the media content lifecycle (production, editing, publication and redistribution), applying to government and private media entities, digital content platforms including cross-border platforms targeting audiences in Saudi Arabia, and content creators. It sets eight principles, among them disclosure of AI-generated or AI-modified content at publication, information integrity, privacy, prevention of misleading content and deepfakes, human responsibility, neutrality, technical security and intellectual-property protection. It also sets handling mechanisms for violations: reporting through approved channels, halting dissemination of non-compliant content, and cooperation with the authorities.

instruments.english_title: Framework for AI-Supported Teaching and Learning Design
instruments.issuing_authority: National eLearning Center (NeLC)
instruments.current_status: Listed on NeLC's studies and publications page, which links the PDF on NeLC's content store. Cover: document type framework, classification public, version 1.0, September 2026.
instruments.summary: NeLC framework (version 1.0, September 2026) giving a practical method for designing AI-supported teaching and learning in general education, higher education, training and lifelong learning. It rests on five principles (learning first, clear educational value, human-centred design, responsible design, evidence-based improvement) and six linked phases, from defining learning outcomes to allocating roles between learner, educator and AI, designing assessment in light of AI use, and verifying and improving the design. It complements NeLC's earlier AI standards, competencies and controls.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Searched SDAIA, CST, NCA, SAMA, SFDA, SASO, Istitlaa and the Bureau of Experts; no AI-specific procurement rules, AI regulatory sandbox, or AI treaty ratification located. "Not found" does not prove absence. Technical review notes: Pilot deep review. sdaia.gov.sa and laws.boe.gov.sa block automated access; dates verified through the Saudi Press Agency, Istitlaa, NCA, SASO and SFDA. Not recorded (out of category scope): National Occupational Standards Framework for Data & AI; Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications. Leads awaiting an official document: AI Principles in Media (Ministry of Media with SDAIA, 2026). Ministry catch-up 2026-10-13 (PROTOCOL §2 ministry rule, applied after this country's deep review; one agent, 30 minutes, national ministries' own AI documents only, nothing else re-reviewed): 5 record(s) added. Ministries: Ministry of Education (schools): Guidelines for the Use of Generative AI in General Education, with SDAIA, 2025-01-24 (recorded); Education / National eLearning Center: AI-Supported Teaching and Learning Design Framework 2026-09, AI and Digital Education roadmap 2025, AI competencies 2025 (recorded); GenAI controls in digital education and prompt-engineering guide (leads, no stated date); Higher education / research: no separate Ministry of Education AI document found (Saudi Academic Framework for AI Qualifications is SDAIA-hosted, not a ministry document); Ministry of Health: nothing AI-specific found (only data governance and open-data policies of the Sectorial Health AI & Data Management Office); Ministry of Justice / Supreme Judicial Council / Public Prosecution: nothing found; Board of Grievances: Principles for the Use of AI Systems (lead; site unreachable, no date read); Ministry of Defense: nothing found; Ministry of Finance / ZATCA: nothing found (ZATCA website disclaimer on AI-generated content only); Ministry of Interior: nothing found; Ministry of Foreign Affairs: no own AI document (US-Saudi Strategic AI Partnership, Nov 2025, is international; see needs_review); Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (labour, civil service): nothing found (news only); Ministry of Media: AI Principles in Media 2026 (recorded; promoted from lead); Ministry of Islamic Affairs: Friday-sermon directive on AI use only (not an instrument); Ministries of Hajj, Culture, Commerce, Tourism, Transport, Energy, Environment, Industry, Municipalities, Economy, Investment, MCIT: nothing found in site-restricted searches; Digital Government Authority (public administration): no AI-specific document found. Not reached: Board of Grievances site (bog.gov.sa) refused connections; Ministry of Media site (media.gov.sa) refused connections; other ministries checked by search only, not by browsing each site. Could not verify: Board of Grievances AI principles: bog.gov.sa unreachable by curl (connection reset) and WebFetch (503).; AI Principles in Media: exact launch date (February 2026 at the Saudi Media Forum per news) not found on an official page; year only recorded.; Ministry of Education guide PDF has no extractable text; content verified from rendered pages and the ministry's news page..
